page: Amazon Web Services c5a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance engineered for parallel, high-throughput computational workloads. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance features an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor delivering 48 physical cores and 96 virtual cores operating at a base clock of 3.3 GHz. The hardware architecture incorporates 192 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a strict 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server carries no local storage, requiring network-attached storage for disk operations, and includes no dedicated hardware graphics acceleration. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate substantial throughput under multi-threaded and cryptographic workloads. Benefiting from native AES and SHA instruction sets, the server achieves top-tier results in cryptographic calculations. Multi-threaded software compilation in Clang, ray tracing, and Redis SET operations also register strong scores. Conversely, per-core processing is limited; the AMD Zen 2 microarchitecture yields modest results in single-threaded tests, including a low-tier stress-ng single-core score and median performance in single-threaded compression.

The 1:2 resource profile presents a cost-efficient footprint for compute-dense applications that do not require high memory density or low-latency local NVMe arrays. Given its substantial core count and 20 Gbps network capacity, AWS c5a.24xlarge is suited for continuous integration build fleets, distributed batch computing, static web traffic handling, and horizontally scaled application backends.
description: Amazon Web Services c5a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 48-core, 96-thread AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at 3.3 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio, it provides 192 GB of DDR4 memory alongside 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance omits local ephemeral storage and dedicated GPU hardware, requiring attached Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent data. In benchmark evaluations, the platform demonstrates top-tier cryptographic execution driven by hardware AES and SHA instructions, as well as strong throughput in multi-core Clang compilation and ray tracing. However, single-core processing capabilities remain lower, ranking in the bottom decile on synthetic stress tests. The instance is suitable for scale-out parallel computing, software build pipelines, distributed microservices, and compute-intensive batch processing.
